$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})=1 \\ x=\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3})(\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10})=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}} \frac{1}{10 x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}\int_{\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10}}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{30}}{10}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{3})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}(\frac{3 \sqrt{10}}{10})\int_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}\int_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(1)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(\frac{\pi}{4})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{360}\end{aligned}

$$
\int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{3}{3 x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x

$$
3 x^{2} + 64=64(1+(\frac{3}{64})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{8}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ x=\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8})(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{3}{3 x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}\int_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{64}(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\int_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}^{1} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(\frac{\pi}{6})) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{3} \pi}{96}\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "b7e7efd8-4daf-5a99-9901-08530da7dbd2" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "b7e7efd8-4daf-5a99-9901-08530da7dbd2" :question/answer-fields $$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] ["8d27d9cf-cb74-5840-b365-e7db0c04fb39" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=3 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(3)(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{1}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=(3)(\frac{1}{6})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 7\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{6}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(3 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 7(\frac{1}{3})\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7}{3}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7}{3}[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  &= \frac{7}{3}(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= \frac{7}{3}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{7 \pi}{18}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["8d27d9cf-cb74-5840-b365-e7db0c04fb39" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["8d27d9cf-cb74-5840-b365-e7db0c04fb39" :question/answer-fields "b6d7a1bb-2b22-5fcb-95fb-9f44edd34200"] $$

$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{8}{36 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 8(\frac{1}{6})\int_{0}^{3} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}\int_{0}^{3} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4}{3}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{3} \\  &= \frac{4}{3}(\operatorname{arctan}(3)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4}{3}((\operatorname{arctan}{\left(3 \right)})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{4 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(3 \right)}}{3}\end{aligned}

$$

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{2}{x^{2} + 6}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] ["e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 6=6(1+(\frac{1}{6})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(0)=0 \\ x=3 \sqrt{2}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6})(3 \sqrt{2})=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{2}{x^{2} + 6}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}\int_{0}^{3 \sqrt{2}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{6} x}{6})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}(\sqrt{6})\int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}(\operatorname{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}((\frac{\pi}{3})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{6} \pi}{9}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["e251937d-16b7-5326-a140-cdc3ea29c25f" :question/answer-fields "0f025f07-d47b-5049-b3e3-da3e27c754f9"] {{answer}}"] ["21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 10=10(1+(\frac{1}{10})x^{2})

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(0)=0 \\ x=\sqrt{10}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(\sqrt{10})=1\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\sqrt{10}} \frac{8}{x^{2} + 10}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{10}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(\sqrt{10})\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{1} \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\operatorname{arctan}(1)-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{10}}{5}((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \pi}{5}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531" :question/answer-fields "5a9796b7-f543-5dc8-b952-8b55e73eb6a2"] [17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "21a4ebc8-c316-5cfd-93e4-ca1118604531"] ["cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/id #uuid "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] ["cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98" :answer/value "\pi"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/id #uuid "b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/key "answer"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/choices "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] ["b352b4d8-ef8e-542f-94af-6fac013fa473" :answer-field/correct "cf36209d-dd8d-57a1-a765-f750e1391b98"] ["561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/id #uuid "561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae"] ["561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] ["561f8902-181d-50e5-8116-48d2cb1ddaae" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{10 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{10(1-(\frac{1}{10})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{10})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(0)=0 \\ x=\sqrt{5}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})(\sqrt{5})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} \frac{4}{\sqrt{10 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{10})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}(\sqrt{10})\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 4[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} \\  &= 4(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 4((\frac{\pi}{4})-(0)) \\  &= \pi\end{aligned}

{{answer}}"] ["b8ad7c5d-7e92-54a2-a9ba-2d3f25475100" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 64=64(1+(\frac{1}{64})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{8}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{8},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(8)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Change both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{8})(0)=0 \\ x=\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=(\frac{1}{8})(\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{6}{x^{2} + 64}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{32}\int_{0}^{\frac{8 \sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+(\frac{x}{8})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{32}(8)\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{4}\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}} \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{4}[\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}} \\  &= \frac{3}{4}(\operatorname{arctan}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})-\operatorname{arctan}(0)) \\  &= \frac{3}{4}((\frac{\pi}{6})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{\pi}{8}\end{aligned}
$$"] ["b8ad7c5d-7e92-54a2-a9ba-2d3f25475100" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["b8ad7c5d-7e92-54a2-a9ba-2d3f25475100" :question/answer-fields "8b06cdcb-17e2-5614-8223-3a8a95be3cd8"] [17592186064220 :knowledge-point/questions "b8ad7c5d-7e92-54a2-a9ba-2d3f25475100"] ["dd1c91ab-c520-5c89-9666-8520331af451" :answer/id #uuid "dd1c91ab-c520-5c89-9666-8520331af451"] ["dd1c91ab-c520-5c89-9666-8520331af451" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["dd1c91ab-c520-5c89-9666-8520331af451" :answer/value "\frac{7 \pi}{3}"] ["c9da6c61-240b-51b8-87c9-710e48d7bbfa" :answer-field/id #uuid "c9da6c61-240b-51b8-87c9-710e48d7bbfa"] ["c9da6c61-240b-51b8-87c9-710e48d7bbfa" :answer-field/key "answer"] ["c9da6c61-240b-51b8-87c9-710e48d7bbfa" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] ["c9da6c61-240b-51b8-87c9-710e48d7bbfa" :answer-field/choices "dd1c91ab-c520-5c89-9666-8520331af451"] ["c9da6c61-240b-51b8-87c9-710e48d7bbfa" :answer-field/correct "dd1c91ab-c520-5c89-9666-8520331af451"] ["a3b89a57-caff-5fb6-834c-90a2ee3c5896" :question/id #uuid "a3b89a57-caff-5fb6-834c-90a2ee3c5896"] ["a3b89a57-caff-5fb6-834c-90a2ee3c5896" :question/problem "Evaluate the integral. {{answer}}"] ["a3b89a57-caff-5fb6-834c-90a2ee3c5896" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$

Both transformed endpoints lie strictly between $-1$ and $1$, so the integrand is continuous throughout the interval.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int_{0}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{7}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{7}{3}\int_{0}^{\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{7}{3}(3)\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 7\int_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 7[\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}]_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\  &= 7(\operatorname{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}(0)) \\  &= 7((\frac{\pi}{3})-(0)) \\  &= \frac{7 \pi}{3}\end{aligned}

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.

$$
